title: Kinetic² (uncommitted kin-22e fix): before a Hard junction the sampled state freezes at a bogus value (p jumps 0.23 at 1 ms, returns at 275 ms)
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef) against the working tree on 2026-10-06 (include/kinetic2/{engine,solver,sources,types}.hpp modified, uncommitted). wasm built with -include algorithm (see below). Defaults, authored ahead, flags 0. reset(0.1, 0); one C1 knot v=0 at (600 ms, 0.5). Samples: 1..~274 ms p 0.331056 v 2.40857 a 0 held constant (dp/dt 0 while v reads 2.41); at 275 ms p is back near 0.1 and the real motion runs, landing at 0.5 at 600 ms at rest. The minimum position no longer winds up below the start (kin-f1t item 1 fixed), but the state before the head starts is wrong: a 0.231 position step at 1 ms and another back at 275 ms. Staircase (five C1 v=0 steps from 0.1 every 300 ms) shows the same at every step (1 ms: p 0.186 v 1.269; 300 ms: p 0.336 v 1.269, dp/dt 86). Looks like Piece::at() for t before the hard head's start returns a clamped or extrapolated head state instead of the hold. Also: solver.hpp uses std::max without #include <algorithm>; the emscripten build (cmake --build build-wasm --target kinetic2_wasm) fails with 4 errors at solver.hpp:398, 584, 591.
notes: Cause: Piece::at computed tau from an unsigned difference, so a time before the piece's start wrapped and returned the END state; a hard-stop head from rest (which now starts later than the origin) showed its launch state for the whole hold. Fixed: before its start a piece holds its start state. <algorithm> included in solver.hpp. check.mjs staircase and hardstop pass with the real module.
close_reason: Piece::at hold-before-start fixed; algorithm include added; presets green.

title: Kinetic² streamed submits teleport the carriage: a stretched knot re-solves at the re-plan origin in zero time (position step up to 0.1 window, jerk 20x jmax)
description:
Found by the playground (kin-8ef), reproduced in bare node against build-wasm/wasm/kinetic2.wasm with no solved() reads (no observer effect). Defaults (vmax 3, amax 30, jmax 500, Blend, floor 0.25, react 4 ms, lookahead 250 ms). reset(0.2, 0); every 100 ms from now=0 submit a free C2 knot 100 ms ahead (t=100..500 ms, p=0.3..0.7); sample at 1 ms.
Trace: submit@0 knot(100,0.3) solves to t 244.4 ms, share 0.25, stretched 144 ms. submit@100 knot(200,0.4): the pending window shows the first knot at t 104 ms (= now + react) p 0.2097 v 0 a 0. Samples: 100 ms p 0.1809 v -0.332; 104 ms p 0.2097 v 0 (p step +0.030). Same at 204 ms (+0.054) and 404 ms (+0.099, from v -0.807 to 0). Knots after the step are reported DeadlineStretched 8.000 s (the cap) then PlanFailed detail 1e30 (kIllegal) and dropped.
Reading: in submit() the re-plan commits the curve to tr and sets origin = piece.at(tr), but the re-solve places the still-pending stretched knot at its authored time (100 ms, now behind the origin) clamped to the origin, so the piece to it has zero duration and the origin jumps to the knot's state. Its earlier stretch is forgotten on re-solve.
Also seen: 60 Hz streamed 1 Hz sine (amplitude 0.35, well inside every ceiling) at 16 ms latency: p step 0.152 -> 0.115 at 305 ms, |j| 10961 vs jmax 500, 830 anomalies over 60 knots. Ahead-authored versions of the same knots have no steps and stay under jmax. Playground presets Scrub and Starved stream show it; playground/check.mjs lists them as expected failures citing this bead.
notes: Fixed 2026-10-06 in the kernel (uncommitted at the time of this note, see the commit that references this id): samples persist their solved time and junction across re-solves (Prior), the first sample keeps the committed curve, new samples sit at an eased 0.9x spacing so the lag closes at the tail, interior samples take min-jerk junctions. Playground scrub and starved presets pass check.mjs with the real module.
close_reason: Streamed re-plan no longer jumps: Prior persistence + replay compression; check.mjs scrub/starved green.

title: Kinetic² never catches up on a dense stream once one knot is infeasible: a 60 Hz 1 Hz sine from rest crawls for 2 s at jmax 500
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). Knots p = 0.5 - 0.35 cos(2 pi t) at 60 Hz from rest at 0.15, defaults (vmax 3, amax 30, jmax 500, Blend floor 0.25). The cosine starts with a = 13.8 u/s^2, so the first knot cannot be met from rest under jmax (about 28 ms of ramp). Expected: a few tens of ms of lag, then tracking. Observed p every 250 ms: 0.150 0.158 0.176 0.201 0.222 0.263 0.296 0.325 0.378 (target 0.15 0.5 0.85 0.5 0.15 ...), the same authored ahead, streamed with KINETIC2_KNOT_SAMPLE (16 ms latency: ... 0.404), under Stretch, and on the previous kernel (not a regression). The same sine at 10 Hz tracks exactly (0.150 0.502 0.850 0.500 0.150 ...), and at jmax 5000 the 60 Hz one tracks. Reading: each later knot is judged from the lagging state and spent again (stretch shifts every later knot, Blend trims toward the previous end), so the lag compounds instead of closing. 60 Hz is the funscript scrub rate. Playground preset Scrub shows it.
notes:
2026-10-06: the crawl was the kernel's stream model, not the sine: with the stream replay (persisted samples, eased compression, min-jerk interior junctions, free tail velocity with a resting acceleration) the 60 Hz sine at jmax 500 should track after its infeasible first knots; re-measure with the real module and close if it does.
2026-10-06 re-measured with the stream model (bare kernel, 60 Hz 1 Hz sine of 0.35 from rest, streamed at 16 ms latency): jmax 500 still crawls (98 of 120 samples refused, peak speed 1.08 of 2.2); jmax 1000 and 5000 track with zero refusals. A piece's jerk at 60 Hz is about 300,000 times the mismatch between its mean speed and its end speeds, so a one-percent speed inconsistency saturates 5000 and a sixth of a percent saturates 500: the ceiling binds, not the model. The playground default is jmax 2000 and the README states the bound. Left open for the operator: document as the floor for 60 Hz streams, or lower the stream rate under 1000.

title: Kinetic² Hard junction winds up backward (to the window edge) before the stroke; a script's last free knot lands moving and the brake overshoots it
description:
Found by the playground (kin-8ef), defaults, authored ahead (all knots submitted at 0), bare-node repro against kinetic2.wasm.
(1) Hard junction wind-up: reset(0.1, 0); one C1 knot v=0 at (600 ms, 0.5). The carriage first moves AWAY from the target: p min 0.0000 at 258 ms (the window edge), v min -0.671, then rises to 0.5. From reset(0.3): p min 0.0488 at 300 ms, v min -1.446, a 0.25 window reversal for a 0.2 stroke. The same move as a free C2 knot has no reversal (p min 0.1 at 0 ms). Suspect the polynomial head to (head_us, head) is fitted with a high head velocity in a short span, and the quintic from rest reaches it by winding up. The Staircase preset (five C1 v=0 steps of 0.15 every 300 ms from 0.1) dips to 0.0992 before its first step, the same effect small.
(2) Last free knot: reset(0.1); one free C2 knot at (600 ms, 0.5): the solver gives it v 0.667, the timeline then runs dry and SettleEngaged brakes past it to 0.5243 (overshoot 0.024). Same at the end of the Hard stop preset (0.9 lands moving at 0.667, brakes to 0.9243) and Overreach under Stretch (0.95 to 0.998). Whether the newest knot of an authored window should be solved to rest is a ruling: the engine comment calls the brake 'the only honest rendering' for a starved stream, but here nothing was starved, the script simply ended.
notes: Both fixed 2026-10-06: (1) a hard-stop knot from rest holds, launches at the latest legal moment and brakes onto the knot (test: a lone hard stop from rest holds, launches and lands); (2) a free last segment rests (Knot::rest_if_last from knotFromSegment, SPEC 9.6; the playground sets the flag in authored mode).
close_reason: Hard-stop hold prefix and rest-if-last landed with tests.

title: Corner option: C1 moving junctions render the author's cubic acceleration step as a jerk-limited ramp (RFC-105 planner option, A/B against continuous)
description: Operator ruling 2026-10-05: both renderings until the tuner proves which earns it. Config::corner = Continuous (default, today's behavior) | Cubic: at an authored C1 knot with nonzero velocity, the acceleration on each side is the C1 Hermite cubic's own at that knot (left: from the incoming span, right: from the outgoing span), joined by one constant-jerk phase of |a_right - a_left| / jmax seconds centered on the knot; the knot is hit at its time with its velocity; the head piece targets the ramp's start state and the next piece starts from its end state. Referee and spends apply to the head; the ramp is legal by construction once |a| <= amax (clamp the side accelerations to amax, EndVelClamped-style report). Fingerprint must not change under the default.
close_reason: Landed as Config::corner with a test pinning the side accelerations to the cubic's own and the ramp jerk to jmax; default Continuous, fingerprint unchanged

title: Kinetic² anomaly reporting: every re-solve re-reports each pending knot's spend; solver anomalies carry the knot's time, not the engine clock; ABI dropped flag is never observable
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). (1) solveWindow reports WaveformScaled/DeadlineStretched for every pending knot on every re-solve, so a streamed knot is reported once per submit while it is pending: 18 anomalies for 5 knots (starved stream), 830 for 60 (streamed scrub). types.hpp says 'one event per axis spent, so the counts read as a diagnosis'. (2) Anomaly::t_us is documented 'engine time at record', but solver kinds record the knot's solved time (e.g. 8304 ms = authored + the 8 s stretch cap, while the clock was at 200 ms); only SettleEngaged and KnotRefused carry the clock. (3) PlanFailed detail is the worst ceiling ratio (1e30 = kIllegal for no legal piece), not only the types.hpp sentinels. (4) ensureSolved erases dropped knots from the timeline and compacts sol[], so kinetic2_solved never returns dropped = 1; a reader can only learn of a drop from PlanFailed (target = authored p). The playground matches drops by that target.
notes: 2026-10-06: anomalies now report once per knot and kind (engine-side mask keyed by the knot's authored time). PlanFailed's detail is documented as a sentinel OR the last attempt's worst ratio. Anomaly t_us is the knot's time (documented). The dropped byte in the ABI stays 0 by construction: the engine erases dropped knots; the PlanFailed anomaly is the record.
